$trace.description: Cancellation, including the branch that matters most: the one where the child's exit cannot be confirmed. Both endings are legitimate contract outcomes, and an implementation that only produces the clean one has not implemented cancellation -- it has implemented the happy path and will misreport the other.

steps.notes: 202 records intent and closes admission. confirmed_exit is fixed false on this response: the platform has accepted the request, not observed a stop.
Same intent, same command ID, no second cancellation and no new grace window. This is what makes repeated cancellation safe for a client that lost the first response.
Cancellation reaches the host through durable state, not an in-memory signal, so it survives a host restart mid-cancellation. The control response conveys status and no authority.

steps.action: send cancel frame with a bounded grace period
steps.notes: intentional is fixed true, tying the stop to the recorded command rather than to a crash.

steps.action: observe child exit within the grace period
steps.notes: Only an observed exit permits recovery_required false.

steps.action: grace period expires with no confirmed exit
steps.notes: The distinct code and recovery_required true keep the uncertainty visible. Claiming a clean cancellation here would leave a possibly-live process working on a task the platform has closed, with nothing in the record asking anyone to check.
A cancelled task never reports a completed result, in either branch. fixtures/invalid/task-snapshot-cancelled-claiming-completion.json is the rejection that pins this.
